text: As the Patriots prepare for their Week 2 home opener against the Steelers on Sunday at 1 PM ET, the organization honored one of its all-time great defensive players when Stephon Gilmore, the 2019 NFL Defensive Player of the Year and two-time All-Pro cornerback, signed a one-day contract on Friday to retire as a New England Patriot, cementing his legacy as one of the finest corners in franchise history. On the injury front, there's some good news and some uncertainty: RB TreVeyon Henderson, who missed the opener with an ankle injury, said Thursday he's "ready to go" and is expected to return, but starting CB Carlton Davis III remains officially questionable after his own injury issues, potentially leaving the secondary vulnerable against Pittsburgh's offense. Meanwhile, the Patriots are looking to bounce back after their opening loss, with Drake Maye and company facing a Steelers team that's rolling early in the season, and in a bit of lighter fare, Pro Football Hall of Famer Adam Vinatieri will be kicking off the team's promotional push for their upcoming game in Munich by attempting a Guinness World Record kick at Jungfraujoch in the Swiss Alps.
